title: Dhyana & Samadhi
description: Journey into the highest stages of yoga, exploring the profound states of meditative absorption where the observer and the observed become one.

sutra.meaning: When there's a sense of effortless linkage of the attention to a particular region in the mind or to the emotions or to a higher dimension, it is the highest stage of yoga, that of samadhi. This is experienced as illumination of the higher self while the yogi feels as if devoid of his conditioned self.

sections.insight: When the seer and the seen appear to merge it is a state of samadhi.  Artists of all kinds when totally engrossed in their art would likely experience such a state. But an artist puts in a lot of effort in his art to reach such a state and is also not able to sustain it in his day to day life. The yogi on the other hand, who has lost the "i" ness seamlessly flows into it.
sections.reflectionPrompt: Have I experienced moments of samadhi in my practice?
sections.practice: Work at something you love with 100% attention and observe your mood afterwards

sections.wisdomFrom: Where the mind rests restrained by the practice of yoga, and where the self seeing the Self is delighted in the Self; and where established, the yogi knows that bliss which transcends the senses, which is understandable by the purified intellect only, and from the experience of Self does not even move; possessing which, he does not think any other gain greater than that; in which established he is not shaken even by great sorrow; that should be known by the term yoga, and that yoga which is free from sorrow should be attained by the undesponding and determined mind.
sections.gurudevInsight: People steal many things, someone else’s poem, some one elect techniques, things. The effect of non-stealing, if you are committed to be sincere, non-stealing – sarvaratnopalapati - all the wealth comes to you effortlessly, all the wealth comes to you. A little intention to steal can keep you poor. A person wants to be sneaky & try to get, grab as much as he can, that is where his luck goes down the drain. Brahmacharayapratisthayam veeryalaabha d) Brahmacharya: - Said as Celibacy. Celibacy brings you strength; a lot of strength but Brahmacharya has a deeper or bigger meaning than just celibacy. [PDF p.84]

sutra.meaning: Practice and detachment can make one experience samadhi in four ways- i) Vitarka ,self-analysis, wherein one logically understands the 'Self' and experiences a shift within. ii) Vichara, synthesis of the senses and thought which brings about 'an awareness' without any disturbance iii) Ananda, bliss iv)  Asmita, only the experience of 'I am'

sections.insight:
It can be a gradual movement from one to the other or any one of the way. 
This is  Samprajnata Samadhi wherein there is still, distinction between the seer and the seen.
sections.reflectionPrompt: Do I need to rationally understand the process or am willing to sit for meditation and let go?

sections.journalPrompt: What do I feel in silence?
sections.wisdomFrom: Better than mechanical practice is knowledge; better than knowledge is meditation. Better than meditation is renunciation of the fruits of actions, for peace immediately follows such renunciation.
sections.gurudevInsight: Suddenly white light coming down – they say Oh!, Something has come down, something is happening – people get misled by such experiences, such evangelic experiences. All this evangelic experiences you should know they are all from sanskara sheshas, some sanskaras from the past, that is a different type of samadhi, hmm. (10) “Bhavpratyayo videha prakrutilayanaam” this goes more into an esoteric life. Samadhi is not a property of just this level of existence. People who do not have body, they too can get affected by the Meditation. [PDF p.21]

sections.theme: Dissolution of all save the Self

sutra.meaning: Asamprajnat-Samadhi is the other kind of Samadhi which is attained by the constant practice of cessation of all mental modifications, in which the Chitta retains only the unmanifested impression.

sections.insight: This state is akin to the state just before falling asleep. The intelligence dissolves but the sense of self remains.
sections.reflectionPrompt: Am I close to stopping the modulations of the mind to some extent?
sections.practice: Intensify your practices to quiten the mind.
sections.gurudevInsight: Then that connection is broken, then it doesn’t happen. Without a gap, constant reminder, constant practice is essential. Just like you go to gymnasium for a couple of days & leave it & go for next month couple of days, nothing will happen. You learn to play a piano, two days you do it, you play & then you leave it for two months & then start playing. You know then there is no consistency, lack of consistency. So a longer time (dirghkaal) without a gap (nairantarya) with honour & respect (satkarsevito), not with grumbling, gaping doing something. [PDF p.14]

sections.theme: The consciousness is freed of all disturbance.

sutra.meaning: In Asamprajnat Samadhi the sadhak may experience bodilessness or become merged in nature leading to solitude.

sections.insight: In this samadhi the sadhak is freed from all modulations but the samskaras spring back to life the moment he comes out of this state.
sections.reflectionPrompt: Am I open to this kind of experience yet?
sections.practice: Intensify your practices to quiten the mind.
sections.gurudevInsight: Before this earth eats you up, become free, free from this feverishness that is gripping your mind, free from this craving for happiness. Every object of pleasure that you have experienced have become Styrofoam, hasn’t it? You know Styrofoam, you eat – what taste it has, isn’t it? Look into every craving that you have, closely, carefully & remember you are going to die. You are craving for sweets, sugar, food - have tons of them, okay have it. The best of the places, you’ll forget them. [PDF p.17]

sutra.meaning: Practice must be persued with faith,confidence, energy, keenness of memory and the power to absorb to avoid spiritual complacency.

Next sutra: Sa tu dirghkaal nairantarya satkarsevito drudbhoomi This effort to be steady,the effort to be still is practice. For a moment you realize, this is this moment & then that vanishes from your sight. But the moment you have said now, then again you have lost the now. sections.theme: Ultimate goal is the supreme divinity.

sutra.meaning:
The Chitta ie consciousness may be totaly focused and surrendered to God.
Ishvara is untouched by suffering and karma

sections.insight: The divine is pure and unaffected. The purpose of human life is to reach that state.

sections.gurudevInsight: Now Patanjali in the next sutra very beautifully analyzes, what is that state of consciousness? That consciousness is free from misery or suffering. Kleshakarmavipakashayerparamrusta purushvishesh ishwara. That core of consciousness, which is free from suffering. Five types of sufferings he enunciates 1. Ignorance: - When your consciousness is filled with ignorance, then there is restlessness, there is unhappiness, suffering. [PDF p.26]

sections.theme: One way is by sound vibrations.

sutra.meaning:

sections.insight:

Repetition deepens experience.

There is no breakage of time as far as it is concerned. I think there was something in Bible – I was before Abraham. Same thing Krishna also says, he say’s I have taught to Ishwaku & Manu. sections.wisdomFrom: God is Omniscient, the most ancient One, the Controller, subtler than the subtlest, the Support of all, and the possessor of an inconceivable divine form; He is brighter than the sun, and beyond all darkness of ignorance. One who at the time of death, with unmoving mind attained by the practice of Yog, fixes the prāṇ (life-airs) between the eyebrows, and steadily remembers the Divine Lord with great devotion, certainly attains Him.
sections.gurudevInsight: When this feeling of elevation, totality of consciousness coming to the core of your existence comes to you, then witness consciousness dawns in you, a different form of consciousness happens in you, your mind gets totally transformed, clarity begins in your thinking, clarity begins in your feelings, the whole body undergoes a transformation. So alive & full of prana & all the 31 obstacles gets removed from your way. Just the memory of the Lordship, of the Divine can remove obstacles from your way. “Vyadhisathyaanasanshaypranadaalasyaviratibrantidarshanalabhdabhoomitvanavasth itatva” 1) Vyadhi means illness in the body is one obstacle, first obstacle. [PDF p.31]

sections.theme: Another way is through focus on something.

sutra.meaning: Meditate on an object of your choice which is spiritually uplifting to you

sections.insight: Any sincere focus leads inward. This method of meditation by Patanjali in this group is seemingly the simplest but actually the hardest. Meditating on ones', self which is of course the most pleasant object to everyone, is the simplest and also the most difficult.
sections.reflectionPrompt: What inspires me?
sections.practice: Meditate at a chosen spot focusing within.
sections.gurudevInsight: By this also your mind becomes calm & one pointed, one focused, hmm! Another Sutra: “vishayvati va pravrutirutpanna manastithinibandhani” Suppose this doesn’t work, it does work but if you feel that still little incompletion is there, then through any one object of senses, the mind can be stilled, you are gazing, what is happening in gazing? You are looking at somebody, for a few moments, you gaze from all your heart, your mind that time is not running here & there. We do the kirtan, singing, after singing, after Bhajan, we sit quiet, meditate, the mind has come to a standstill, isn’t it? 40 We have done the Grape process in the Basic course. [PDF p.40]

sections.theme: The smallest to the largest  are all within the purview.

sutra.meaning: Mastery extends from smallest to largest

sections.insight: Awareness expands limitlessly. Maharishi Patanjali has given various methods of dhyan or meditation  to master ones chitta or cosciousness and stop the desires from overtaking the mind.
sections.reflectionPrompt: Where can I expand awareness?
sections.gurudevInsight: What is the sign of progress in Meditation? “Parmanuparatmahatvaantosya vashikaar” From the smaller than the smallest, to the bigger than the biggest comes within his preview of operation. Then Nature loves you, start supporting you. From the atom - smaller than the smallest to the bigger than the biggest comes with in your preview of operation on life. [PDF p.46]

sections.theme: Purity of mind is the aim.

sutra.meaning: When the seer the seen and the instrument of perception become one, the mind becomes clear and it reflects reality like a crystal

sections.insight:
When the mind is pure it reflects truth without distortion.This is a very refined state of consciousness called samapatti. 
Thus yoga and samadhi are but means to reach the state of samapatti.
sections.reflectionPrompt: Is my perception clear or colored?
sections.gurudevInsight: If you do this, you chita, your mind will be pleasant. In that gracious, graceful mind, one pointedness becomes very much easy, very simple, hmm! Practice one thing or devotion to one thing or one aspect. Ok, Even that becomes difficult, he says, there is another sutra. “Prachardanvidharanbhya va pranasya” Breaking the rhythms of the breath, the natural rhythms of the breath & holding the breath, sustaining the breath in different rhythms. If someone asks you, where did Patanjali talked about kriya, Patanjali has not mentioned about Sudarshan kriya directly. [PDF p.40]

sutra.meaning: Savitarka samapatti wherein perception words, their meaning simultaneously blend with understanding into a special knowledge. .

sections.insight: The sadhaks chitta has become clear like a mirror and there are no boundaries to understanding.
sections.reflectionPrompt: Where do I over-interpret?
sections.gurudevInsight: Every possible obstacle has been counted, included in these 9 categories. Just few words, very few words, very concisely he has said all that in to be said, that was needed to be said. Along with these nine obstacles, the 5 indications or signs of disturbed mind is mentioned i.e. 1) Dukha: Sadness/Sorrow 2) daurmanasya: Bitterness 3) agmajayatva: Restlessness in the body or lack of coordination in the body and 4) shwasprashwas: Irregular breathing. [PDF p.36]

sections.theme: Memory is the grime on the mirror.

sutra.meaning: When memory is purified only truth shines Let go of past filters to see clearly.

sections.insight: Past impressions create biases and prejudices. Unless the slate is continuously cleaned the writing on top will be garbled.
sections.reflectionPrompt: Do I think too much of what has passed. Is my perception colored by past experiences.
sections.gurudevInsight: So that person thinks Oh yes, see I am very miserable. You do not help them in any way to wake up to the truth, its nothing; many people are suffering even more. I am not saying you don’t go or you go & tell them that your suffering is nothing, many people are suffering more. But have compassion for people who are suffering & not friendliness. And People who are doing good job, meritorious jobs, who have lots of merits, who are blessed, feel happy with them, become one with them, feel you are doing that job with them. Then the sense of competition disappears, jealousy subsides, finding faults with people who are doing good things will go away. [PDF p.38]

sutra.meaning: Nature at its subtlest is consciousness. When the two dissolve into one it is at its purest.

sections.insight: Awareness expands beyond form. There is total cessation of the modulations of the small mind and the appearance of the Cosmic Mind or mahat.
sections.reflectionPrompt: Can I go beyond labels?
sections.gurudevInsight: We go and make their belief more strong by saying that God is so unjust with you. Nature is so unkind with you, you are suffering, you are poor thing. We even push them down, even down the drain we are trying to pull them out of the drain but we push them down. Uncousciously we do because we think oh, they are my great friends, what do I do? People who are suffering, do not pity them. See there is a difference between pitying & being compassionate. [PDF p.38]

sections.theme: The intellect needs to dissolve too.

sutra.meaning: These are seed-based meditations, ie the sadhak's intellect or buddhi is still in play.

sections.insight: The six samapattis mentioned viz. savitarka, nirvitarka, savichara, nirvichara , ananda and asmita are all sabeej (or seeded in nature).
sections.reflectionPrompt: What patterns remain?
sections.gurudevInsight: See, you can see the same Self in everybody but the feelings will not be the same. One does not feel the same with everybody though intellectually you may say its myself only there but you’re feelings, since it is not fully cultured, fully established in the Self, it still has its preferences, its ways. Says - be friendly with those who are happy. If you are friendly with unhappy people what happens? So he says don’t be friendly with unhappy people but be compassionate to them. People who are suffering, have sympathy, compassion for them, but don’t hook on to friendliness because then it drags you down and makes you unhappy. [PDF p.37]

sutra.meaning: Nirvichar or non Reflection brings clarity in subtle awareness and inner joy

sections.insight: When the chitta (consciousness) and buddhi (intellect) remain non reflective inner clarity blossoms and brings calm and happiness.
sections.reflectionPrompt: Did I feel inner ease?
sections.gurudevInsight: What happens when you keep doing one thing? The restlessness & boredom takes you to a peak that it brings clarity. Our mind is troubled because it is dwelling on duality. & then it is jumping all around the place. This, that, this, that & the mind is further divided. Divided mind is misery & one pointed mind is Joy. [PDF p.36]

sutra.meaning: Seasoned wisdom arises in the chitta (consciousness) and provides immense insight.

sections.insight: Inner wisdom is beyond logic and human intellect.
sections.reflectionPrompt: Did insight arise naturally?
sections.gurudevInsight: Because mind is like air, is energy, is all pervading. Air does not have a location, it does not fix somewhere & the veetraaga chitta is all permeating, so that is why that air, that cool breeze, that energy enters into your system, because mind is also like ether, your consciousness is ether, is all pervading. “Veetraagavishaya va chittam” But even there if you do raga, Dwesha even there, that’s why it is said that Guru or an enlightened person – don’t see them as a human Being, as a person, its likes & dislikes. [PDF p.43]

sections.theme: Its a different kind of wisdom.

sutra.meaning: This wisdom differs from knowledge gained externally

sections.insight: Direct experience is different from learned knowledge.
sections.reflectionPrompt: Did I experience or just think?
sections.gurudevInsight: If you have to go to my father, you have to go through me; there is no other way, means what – you have to go through the Master because Master is a solid example, because you have to pass your mind, go through your mind & what can help your mind? Is the doorway, is the door, those vibrations, those sensations & those vibrations, sensation manifest in that body where the chitta is, veetraaga - is blossoming fully, fully blossomed without any hindrances – veetraaga vishayamva chittam Next sutra: “Swapnanidragyaanalambavan va” Knowledge of sleep & dreams. You sleep all your life but you have never met your sleep. [PDF p.44]

sections.insight:
Awareness replaces conditioning.
Ultimate stillness is beyond all patterns.
sections.reflectionPrompt:
What pattern shifted?
Can I rest without effort?
sections.gurudevInsight: 1) Dukha: Sadness/Sorrow 2) daurmanasya: Bitterness 3) agmajayatva: Restlessness in the body or lack of coordination in the body and 4) shwasprashwas: Irregular breathing. If you have observed your breath, when you are happy or excited, the incoming breath is longer, you are more aware of the incoming breath in a state of excitement & when you are unhappy, the outgoing breath is more prominent, you observe the outgoing breath, total imbalance of the breath happens. Big sigh, heavy, when you are unhappy, & when you are joyful, you are only breathing & you don’t know when you are breathing out, you are not conscious of out breath. [PDF p.36]

sutra.meaning: Subtle impressions dissolve by returning to source.Meditation removes disturbances

sections.insight: Going inward dissolves patterns.Meditation clears mind patterns.
sections.reflectionPrompt: Can I go inward?Did meditation help?
sections.gurudevInsight: Tanukarna - thin them down, reduce it, reduce it, reduce it to its minimum. When you make them subtle & subtle & subtle, they let you come back to your Self, they bring the mind back to the source. When these miseries are very thick, it bothers you, it captivates your mind. The moment they becomes thinner & thinner, they let your mind free & get it back to its Self, the source. See, when you are craving for somebody a lot, a teenager, or a youth is craving for a girl friend or a boyfriend. When that craving is there, the mind is not settled, it is unable to sit & meditate. [PDF p.70]
